subject.title: feat(fleet): multi-tenant hosting via openclaw fleet cell supervisor

question: Should OpenClaw core own `openclaw fleet` as the supported multi-tenant isolation and lifecycle boundary?
rationale: The feature establishes durable security, persistence, upgrade, and operator API obligations that cannot be accepted from implementation quality alone.

options.title: Own Fleet in core
options.body: Accept the long-term isolation, lifecycle, persistence, and experimental upgrade contract after the defects and proof gaps are resolved.

options.title: Keep orchestration external
options.body: Retain the trust-model documentation but move tenant orchestration to external deployment tooling.

options.title: Pause the direction
options.body: Close or defer the PR if maintainers do not want OpenClaw core to own this boundary.

recommendation.title: Own Fleet in core
recommendation.body: Accept the long-term isolation, lifecycle, persistence, and experimental upgrade contract after the defects and proof gaps are resolved.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the linked design and have adjacent current-main state and Docker history, making them the best available owner for this product-direction decision.
